adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:56 — [P2, confidence 50] Any existing duck-typed installation that implements the previously supported `should_sync(self, attribute)` contract crashes with TypeError because the task admits it through `hasattr` and then always passes a second positional argument, preventing assignee synchronization for that integration; code: `if installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source):

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that duck-typed installations implementing the old `should_sync(self, attribute)` signature will crash. However, looking at the diff, the new parameter `sync_source` has a default value of `None` (`sync_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`). This means the method can still be called with just one argument, and existing implementations that only accept one argument would work fine when called with keyword arguments. The call in the task uses `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` which passes two positional arguments, but this is calling the method on the installation object which is obtained from `integration_service.get_installation`. The base classes `IssueBasicIntegration` and `IssueSyncIntegration` both have the updated signature with the default parameter. Any subclass that overrides `should_sync` would need to be updated, but this is a normal API evolution, not a bug introduced by this diff. The diff shows the method signature change is consistent across the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — [P3, confidence 100] Advisory: `queued` is evaluated once at module import, so this works today only because no consumer reads it but breaks when an age-based retry or loop guard consumes the serialized metadata and treats every fresh assignment source as having the stale process-start timestamp; code: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a default value in a dataclass is evaluated once at module import time, not at instance creation time. This is a well-known Python gotcha with mutable/dynamic default values. Looking at the diff, the `AssignmentSource` dataclass at line 18 uses `timezone.now()` as a default value, which means all instances created without explicitly passing `queued` will share the same timestamp from when the module was first imported. The `to_dict()` method serializes this field, and `from_dict()` deserializes it, so the stale timestamp would propagate through the system. This is a real bug that would cause incorrect timestamps.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug. In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 17, the default value `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at module import time, not at instance creation time. This means all AssignmentSource instances will share the same timestamp from when the module was first imported. The test at line 36 only checks `is not None`, which passes but doesn't verify the timestamp is actually current. This is a known Python gotcha with mutable/callable default arguments in dataclasses.
